title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a handwritten crib sheet ('Formules utiles') that Grothendieck added to his copy of the Deligne–Tate 'Courbes elliptiques : formulaire' (LNM 476, Antwerp IV). It collects the standard facts about modular forms in char p that a Gauss–Manin / Picard–Fuchs / Cartier-operator seminar needs.

(1) Discriminant and j-invariant. The page records 1728Δ = c4^3 − c6^2 and j = c4^3/Δ = 1728 + c6^2/Δ. Here c4, c6, Δ are sections of ω^4, ω^6, ω^12 over the compactified moduli stack \bar{M} (written \bar{Π}). ω is the Hodge line bundle e^*Ω^1.

(2) Automorphisms. In characteristic ≠ 2,3: c4 = 0 ⇔ the curve has 6 automorphisms ⇔ j = 0. Similarly c6 = 0 ⇔ 4 automorphisms ⇔ j = 1728.

(3) Hasse invariant and degree of ω. The Hasse invariant h is a section of ω^{⊗(p−1)} over \bar{M} ⊗ F_p. The degree of ω on the stack is 1/24.

These two facts are implicitly combined. The zero divisor of h is the supersingular locus, so its stacky degree is (p−1)/24 = Σ_{E supersingular} 1/#Aut(E). This is the Eichler–Deuring mass formula. Since the generic automorphism group is ±1, it gives roughly p/12 supersingular j-values.

(4) Tate curve. For E = G_m/q^Z with the canonical differential du/u:
- c4 = (du/u)^4 · E4 = 1 + 240 Σσ3(n)q^n (Ramanujan's Q);
- c6 = (du/u)^6 · E6 = 1 − 504 Σσ5(n)q^n (Ramanujan's R).
The question 'h = (du/u)^{⊗(p−1)} at ∞?' asks whether the Hasse invariant has q-expansion 1 at the cusp. It does: the Tate curve is ordinary and its Hasse invariant is 1 relative to du/u (Deligne; Katz 1973; Serre/Swinnerton-Dyer: E_{p−1} ≡ 1 mod p).

(5) Legendre family. For y^2 = x(x−1)(x−λ), j = 2^8 (1−λ+λ^2)^3/(λ(1−λ))^2. The six λ-values over a given j are listed: λ, 1−λ, λ^{-1}, 1−λ^{-1}, (1−λ)^{-1}, (1−λ^{-1})^{-1}. These correspond to the choices of marked 2-torsion points ('points d'ordre 2 marqués').

(6) Hasse polynomial. In the Legendre parameter it is H_p(λ) = (−1)^n Σ_i C(n,i)^2 λ^i with n = (p−1)/2.

(7) Table of supersingular j-values: p=5: j=0; p=7: j=1728; p=11: j=0 and 1728; in general about p/12 others. The row label 'λ=' should read 'j='.

The page serves the cote's theme: the Hasse invariant viewed as the Cartier operator / Frobenius on H^1, and the Legendre Picard–Fuchs (hypergeometric) equation, whose mod-p polynomial solution is H_p(λ).
errors: Row label in the supersingular table is written 'λ =' but the entries (0, 1728) are j-values, so it should be 'j ='.
c6 and Δ are written with '=' instead of '∈' H^0(\bar{Π}, ω^6), ω^12 (notational slip).

The general count 'p−·/12 autres' is schematic. The exact number of supersingular j is ⌊p/12⌋ + ε with ε ∈ {0,1,2} depending on p mod 12; this is consistent with the mass (p−1)/24 but not stated exactly.
Sign of c6 initially miswritten and corrected to 1 − 504 Σσ5(n)q^n, which is correct.

deep.surprise_reason: A personal crib sheet of well-known formulas: Tate/Deligne formulaire, Hasse invariant, mass formula, Legendre family. The only open 'question' (the q-expansion of h) was already answered in the literature (Deligne/Katz). Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'car ≠ 2,3' is a left-margin note qualifying the c4=0 / c6=0 equivalences.
The Hasse invariant line reads h ∈ H^0(\bar{Π}, ω^{⊗(p−1)}), with a crossed-out exponent.
In the c6 line the operator was overwritten and should read 1 − 504 Σσ5(n)q^n.
'E = G_m/q^Z, du/u →' is a left-side heading for the Tate-curve q-expansions.
In the bottom table the row label 'λ =' should be j-values. The first p-entry is unclear (possibly 3) with no j listed; then p=5: 0, p=7: 1728, p=11: 0 and 1728, '(12)' above, 'et (p−·)/12 autres'.
The bracket near the j-formula reads '[p^ts d'ordre 2 marqués]' (points of order 2 marked).
